Title: Betrayer query for LSJ, or anyone really

Messages.Author: Legbiter
Messages.Body:
Betrayer's text is confusing, IMO. When the Methuselah guesses who the
betrayer is, does s/he have to guess its NAME, or indicate which among the
face-down cards in your crypt is the actual betrayer? How in practise
would this work? Suppose for example that I had several uncontrolled vamps
that another Methuselah had controlled ..... what would stop me saying,
not that one but this one? If I have to say "I have an uncontrolled copy
of Lucian", s/he guesses it's number 2 [wrongly] can i shuffle my
uncontrolleds around and lay them out again before s/he gets another
chance to guess?

Also, Betrayer seems to stack [not a unique master]. So if I have multiple
master phase actions can i play several? And if I play them all on the
same vamp, does the victim Methuselah burn pool for each card, and have to
burn an extra pool to remove each card?

If it IS stackable then it's actually quite a good card! Hitting your prey
for 2-4 with the Recruitment/Betrayer combo would be quite fun.

Also, kudos to Xian's mate for thinking up a viable use for Mercy for the
Weak! Still doesn't work if your rushing opponent is using IG, though.

Messages.Author: ber...@cco.caltech.edu
Messages.Body:
>
> > If it IS stackable then it's actually quite a good card! Hitting your prey
> > for 2-4 with the Recruitment/Betrayer combo would be quite fun.
>
> Yes, I imagine so.
>

Actually, that combo is fairly useless. Recruitment requires you to show the
vampire to all players. *If* you used Recruitment one turn, then had three
master phase actions (Anson or Rumours of Gehenna + Parthenon), you could play
three Betrayers on the next turn. This would cause a maximum of 6 pool loss
to the other methuselah (1 lost and 1 spent for each Betrayer). Since it
takes 2 turns, 4 master phase actions, 2 pool, and needs you to have 2
specific cards in play and 4 in hand at a given time, the combo is hardly
worth the effort. Not to mention that building a deck around it would be
rather silly. Better to play with all the 4-capacity vampires and a few big
guys that a lot of people use and then play lots of Effective Managements,
Kindred Intelligences, and Betrayers. Even then, it's not likely to be much
good. Betrayer can be sort of okay to just throw 1 or 2 in a deck if you're
using lots of common vamps, but other than that, it's mostly useless.

...Now maybe if you used 2 Recruitments and put 3 Betrayers split between 2
vamps and then kept playing them each turn...

-Chris
